title: A Hypothesis-Driven Framework for Detecting Lexical Semantic Change
venue: CLiC-it 2025 (Eleventh Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics), CEUR Workshop Proceedings, pp. 177-185

selection.evidence: Cited as [20] by the SemEval-2027 Task 3 organisers' synthetic-data paper (saponara2026) for the 0.5 clustering threshold; its title matches Subtask 2's name 'Hypothesis-Driven Change Detection'. Opened to learn the organisers' own method for Subtask 2 before building one (arena-lsc ticket 2026-10-31-Baseline).

cost.compute_notes: ACL Anthology PDF, 9 pp, read in full via PyMuPDF. No code or data released with the paper (none referenced). Nothing run.

triggers: how do the SemEval-2027 Task 3 organisers detect usages of one given sense

Janus historical usage generation sense definition
hypothesis-driven lexical semantic change subtask 2 method

claims.statement: Given expert sense definitions, generate synthetic usages per sense with Janus (Llama-3-8B fine-tuned on 1,191,851 OED example sentences), average their XL-LEXEME embeddings into one prototype per sense, and rank corpus usages by cosine to the prototype; the top-ranked usages per period are read by experts to date a sense's emergence.
claims.scope: Three English words (theory, gene, force) in CCOHA; qualitative use case only. No gold labels, no precision/recall, no comparison system with numbers.

our_assessment.why: This is a method description with a demonstration, not an evaluation: Table 2 shows only the single most similar sentence per (sense, year) with cosine 0.88-0.98. Nothing measures how many usages above any threshold actually carry the sense, so it says nothing yet about the F1 such a ranker would get on a binary usage-vs-definition task (which is exactly SemEval-2027 Task 3 Subtask 2). Notably the reported similarities are compressed in 0.88-0.98 even for OCR noise ('genie rose' 0.88 for the metaphorical gene sense), so a fixed cosine threshold would need calibration per word.

claims.statement: Sense clusters for the exploratory part are induced with agglomerative clustering on XL-LEXEME embeddings at a distance threshold of 0.5; JSD over cluster distributions, PRT and APD are computed against the first period.
claims.scope: Settings stated in Section 4 and 4.1; linkage and distance metric not stated.

our_assessment.why: A setting, reported as used. The linkage is unstated, which matters: the same threshold gives very different cluster counts under average vs complete linkage. saponara2026 later reports 0.32 as better for change detection on synthetic data.

relations.why: Cassotti and Tahmasebi on both; saponara2026 cites this paper for the 0.5 threshold.

open_questions: Is Janus public (weights), and does an equivalent exist for SV/IT/ES/NL/RU? Without it the prototype step needs another generator or real dictionary examples.
What F1 does prototype-cosine ranking reach on a sense-annotated set with a fixed threshold vs a per-word threshold? Testable on dwug_de_sense / AXOLOTL in task format (arena-lsc).
